title: Migrate Python file-utility module from os.path to pathlib.Path
description: A small Python file-utility module uses os.path for all path operations. Migrate the three functions to use pathlib.Path while keeping the same external interface and all 5 tests green.

task_spec.prompt:
The module src/file_utils.py implements three functions using os.path and os.listdir:
  - list_text_files(directory: str) -> list[str]: returns sorted .txt filenames in a directory
  - read_if_exists(path: str) -> str | None: returns file contents, or None if missing
  - ensure_dir(path: str) -> str: creates directory tree if absent, returns path

Migrate all three functions to use pathlib.Path internally. Keep the function signatures identical (accept str, return str/list[str]/None). The 5 existing tests must still pass after the migration.

Rules:
- Remove 'import os' when it is no longer needed (keep only what is used)
- Use Path() to wrap the input strings inside each function
- Use Path methods (.iterdir(), .exists(), .is_file(), .is_dir(), .mkdir(), .read_text(), .suffix, etc.) instead of os.path calls
- Do not change the public API (parameter names, return types, behaviour)

Run uv run pytest tests/ -q to confirm all 5 tests still pass.
required_artifacts: list_text_files uses Path.iterdir() instead of os.listdir
read_if_exists uses Path.exists() and Path.read_text() instead of open()
ensure_dir uses Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) instead of os.makedirs
import os removed or reduced to only used symbols
success_criteria: All os.path calls replaced by pathlib equivalents
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
